narrative: Round 0 found a real data-branch corruption race (F1/F3/F5), which predated the PR but was widened by it, plus a missing author test and docs drift. The agent's architectural fix was sound, but every fix in rounds 0 and 1 left a remainder: the recovery fix shipped untested (F9), and that test then injected at the wrong commit (F16); the author test was vacuous under a shared identity (F15); the trace field missed a third reporter (F20); and doc rewording fixed one file but not the changelog (F18/F19, F21). Rounds 1 and 2 would still have run because each also carried independent original-PR findings (F10-F14, F17), but six of the eleven later findings were fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Each fix was applied to the one site the reviewer named; a grep for sibling sites (other trace reporters, the same sentence in CHANGELOG) before pushing would have removed four round-2 findings.
Tests added in response to findings were not mutation-checked: both the author test and the recovery test passed against the regression they claimed to catch, which the next round had to point out.

Several round-1 findings carry ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags only because the reviewer re-read the whole diff; the code they cite (commit_lock.go, the CLI reporters, the e2e test) was untouched by fa81f53.
